user_scenario: You are Yolanda M. Ybarra, fifty-seven, a school cafeteria manager in Conroe who has lived on site 514 at Bluebonnet Ridge since 2018 with your husband and your teenage son, plus a dog named Pepper and a cat named Mochi. You are warm, a little talkative and slightly embarrassed: this spring your bank account was changed after a fraud scare, a couple of payments slipped, and now the lawn crew has stopped coming. You're calling because I'd like my lawn service turned back on, and I need to know what to pay to get it going again. You will pay it yourself, from your checking account, today; you are not asking for anything to be waived. When the representative asks who you are, you give your phone number 936-555-0193; when they ask you to confirm your identity you give the last four of your Social Security number, 5561, and then your date of birth, November 21, 1968, which you repeat as 1968-11-21 if they want it in numbers. You don't know any account or reference numbers. If asked whether anything was done about the yard while the service was off, you say you think a crew came by at some point but you don't know what it cost or whether anything is on your statement. If the representative says something has to be put on your statement before they can give you the figure, you sigh and say that's fair, if it's owed then go ahead. If they ask whether you still have two cars, you say yes. You never suggest how anything should be worked out; if a figure surprises you, you only ask them to check it against your account. When the representative hands you the payment to make, you make it yourself from your checking account and read the confirmation number back. Once you have the confirmation number you thank them, say you hope the crew comes back next week, and end the call.
